resident_loads.doc: ADR 0111 (Lead 2026-10-28: the PC measured New Game 3.0 s, Ch2 2.0 s, the first fight 1.7 s and Ch1 1.3 s in one hidden frame; ADR 0029 allows 1 s). Most of that frame was the hero bodies' first load(): HeroFieldActor.attach and the battle stand-ins read each hero scene from disk on the main thread, inside the swap frame (1.6-2.6 s headless on the cloud box; 6-15 ms once the scenes are cached). ResidentLoads (game/core/resident_loads.gd, installed on SceneRouter) loads these scenes on worker threads (ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request) as soon as a change starts, holds the router's swap (hold_swap, at most PREWARM_WAIT_MAX_FRAMES) until they are in, and keeps them for the session, so a later change pays nothing. The title starts them as soon as it shows (no hold). 'sources' lists where the paths come from: each a JSON file, the key path to a table of rows, and the row key naming the scene; 'party_only' keeps only the rows of heroes in the party (the battle actors, which load the full model) plus 'leader_default'. 'paths' adds fixed paths. A change to a scene in 'no_hold_scenes' starts the loads without holding its swap. 'max_in_flight': how many threaded loads run at once (the rest queue): hundreds at once crashed Godot 4.6.3 (ADR 0029's Haluna crash; this class's test). A zone's own runtime loads come from game/data/ui/scene_loads.json (tools/loading/scene_loads.gd).
